tests.prompt: Start a crypt encounter. Verify exactly one monster (ref dnd5e:monsters:skeleton) is seeded in the entrance region.
Start a crypt encounter. Verify zero monsters are seeded in the corridor region.
Start a crypt encounter. Verify exactly one monster (ref dnd5e:monsters:skeleton-captain, non-wight rpg-toolkit#816) is seeded in the boss region.
Start two crypt encounters with the same explicit RandomSeed. Verify monster positions are byte-identical.
Start crypt encounters with the same seed and party sizes 1, 2, 3, 4. Verify monster positions are identical regardless of party size.
Sweep seeds 1..1000 x party sizes 1..4. Verify zero placement errors across the full matrix.
Verify the crypt monster seeding EntityGroups carry FixedPositions with len==Quantity and PositionOracle==nil — no out-of-sight search/retry path is exercised.
Verify both the entrance and boss anchors resolve to positions Room.CanPlaceEntity accepts (not walls, not out of bounds) and are tagged into their expected region via RegionAt.
Verify the boss anchor is not visible (perception.CanSeeAt) from the entrance anchor while the boss door is closed, using real LoS/wall geometry — not a placement-search predicate.

Call tkenc.CryptDungeonParams directly (not through rpg-api's dungeonSpec) and apply the same production anchor-resolution helper. Verify it composes correctly against the toolkit's own canonical region/door/path shape, independent of PR #697.
Against a real Redis-backed lobby+encounter repo (testcontainers), call StartEncounter twice with the same explicit seed. Verify byte-identical monster positions end to end.
